about.tagline: One store for every Windows app.
about.intro: Unibox brings WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop together into one clear store with {{count}} apps – plus npm, Bun, pip, Cargo, vcpkg, .NET Tool and PowerShell for developers. Install in one click, update in bulk, and stop worrying where an app comes from.
about.hlSourcesText: One app = one page. Choose which manager to install it from.
about.hlOpenText: The source code is public on GitHub – anyone can contribute.
about.hlSafeText: Installs come from official repositories; admin rights only via the UAC prompt.
about.hlLangText: The interface is ready for more languages – just add a translation.
about.techText: Thanks to great open source projects and the communities maintaining the package repositories.
about.communityText: Ideas, bugs and questions are all welcome.
about.disclaimer: Unibox is an independent open source project and is not affiliated with Microsoft or with the package manager projects it supports. Windows, WinGet, .NET, PowerShell and vcpkg are trademarks of Microsoft; Chocolatey is a trademark of Chocolatey Software, Inc.; npm is a trademark of npm, Inc.; Python and PyPI are trademarks of the Python Software Foundation; Rust and Cargo are trademarks of the Rust Foundation. Apps and packages belong to their authors.

publish.title: Publish your app
publish.subtitle: Reach Unibox users alongside {{count}} other apps – no fees and no store of your own.
publish.step1Text: One is enough – apps in WinGet, Chocolatey or Scoop, tools and libraries in npm, PyPI, crates.io, NuGet or the PowerShell Gallery. Unibox has no repository of its own; it shows packages from them.
publish.step2Text: The catalog updates daily. Your app shows up with versions from every source it's available in.
publish.step3Title: Polish your page and get verified
publish.step3Text: Add screenshots, a banner and categories, and confirm the app is yours – you'll get the blue checkmark.
publish.whereSubtitle: Each manager has its own process. WinGet reaches the most users since it ships with Windows.
publish.channel_winget: Create a manifest right in Unibox (or with wingetcreate) and open a pull request to microsoft/winget-pkgs.
publish.channel_chocolatey: Build a .nupkg package and push it to the Chocolatey Community Repository for moderation.
publish.channel_scoop: Add a manifest to the Extras bucket (pull request), or create your own bucket.
publish.channel_npm: Publish the package to the npm registry – Bun installs from it too. Mark command-line tools with the “bin” field in package.json.
publish.channel_pip: Build the package and upload it to PyPI; define command entry points in pyproject.toml.
publish.channel_cargo: Publish the crate to crates.io; binary crates can then be installed with cargo install.
publish.channel_vcpkg: Add a port to the official microsoft/vcpkg registry (pull request), or to your own registry.
publish.channel_dotnet: Pack the tool as a NuGet package with PackAsTool and push it to nuget.org.
publish.channel_pwsh: Publish the module or script to the PowerShell Gallery – both PowerShell 7 and 5.1 can install it.
publish.improveText: Package repositories only hold the basics. Add the rest with a pull request to the Unibox catalog (data-pipeline/rules).
publish.improveBanner: A custom banner and brand color
publish.improveCategories: Categories, tags and a longer description

publish.verifyText: The blue checkmark shows users the app really comes from you, not someone using your name.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Answers to common questions and where to turn when you're stuck

how.a: Unibox doesn't download or modify anything itself. It hands the installation to a package manager – WinGet, Chocolatey, Scoop, or for developer tools npm or pip, for example – and shows its progress. Packages come straight from the official repositories.

source.q: Where is an app installed from when it's in several sources?
source.a: From the first enabled source in the order you set in <settings>Settings</settings>. You can pick the source manually on the app's profile. An installed app is updated through the source it was installed from.

uac.q: Why does the User Account Control (UAC) window appear?
uac.a: Some installers write to system folders and therefore need administrator rights; Chocolatey always requires them. Unibox asks for permission only for that specific operation – it never runs entirely as administrator.

bundles.q: How do I install several apps at once?
bundles.a: Add them to a <bundles>package bundle</bundles> (the plus icon on an app's card). Then install the bundle in one click, save it to a file, or create a PowerShell script for another PC.

failed.a: The <history>operation history</history> shows what failed and lets you retry. Details are in the <logs>package manager logs</logs>. Trying another source or closing an app that blocks the installer often helps.

safe.q: Is installing through Unibox safe? Can I get a virus?
safe.a: Yes – it's the safest way to install apps. Unibox doesn't download programs from random websites with fake “Download” buttons, only from the package managers' official repositories. Microsoft checks WinGet packages (SmartScreen, static analysis) and WinGet verifies the installer's SHA-256 checksum before installing, so a tampered installer won't get through. Chocolatey packages go through moderation and VirusTotal antivirus scanning, and Scoop verifies the checksum from its manifest. Nothing is bundled with the installer and Unibox doesn't modify it. For developer libraries and tools (npm, PyPI, crates.io…) the author is responsible for the content – install them from publishers you trust. Unibox is open source and sends no personal data without signing in.

add.q: An app or source is missing. How do I add it?
add.a: Apps get into Unibox through the package managers' repositories – see the <publish>Publish</publish> page for how. You can suggest a new package source with the “Add source” button in the sidebar.

commands.title: Terminal commands
commands.subtitle: Everything Unibox does with a click, you can also do from the command line. Pick a package manager and copy a command.
commands.howTo: Run the commands in Windows Terminal or PowerShell. The examples use one sample app and can be copied as they are – you'll find the exact command for any other app on its page, in the “… from the command line” section.
commands.howToPlaceholders: Run the commands in Windows Terminal or PowerShell. Replace <package> (<ID> for WinGet) with the package and <name> with what you're looking for – you'll find the exact command for a specific app on its page, in the “… from the command line” section.

note.winget: WinGet comes with Windows 10 and 11 (App Installer). It looks apps up by their exact ID – find it on the app's page or with winget search.
note.chocolatey: Installing, updating and uninstalling with Chocolatey needs a Terminal run as administrator.
note.scoop: Scoop installs into your user folder without admin rights. Apps live in buckets – add “extras” (Firefox, VLC…) with scoop bucket add extras.
note.npm: Global npm packages are command-line tools (TypeScript, ESLint…). npm comes with Node.js.
note.bun: Bun is a fast replacement for Node.js and npm. It adds global packages with bun add -g; updating means installing again with @latest.
note.pip: pip installs Python packages. Run it as python -m pip – that uses the pip of the Python on your PATH. Searching PyPI from the command line isn't possible, use pypi.org.
note.cargo: Cargo is Rust's package manager – cargo install builds a tool from source. The install command also installs a newer version.
note.vcpkg: vcpkg manages C and C++ libraries (classic mode – no vcpkg.json in a project).
note.dotnet: .NET tools (dotnet tool) install globally into your user folder. They need the .NET SDK.
note.powershell: Windows PowerShell 5.1 modules via PowerShellGet (*-Module commands).

settings.title: Settings
settings.themeHint: System follows your Windows setting; if it cannot be detected, the dark theme is used.
settings.supportHint: Unibox is free, with no ads and no subscription – and it'll stay that way. If it saves you time, you can make a voluntary contribution of any amount towards further development.
settings.preferredSourceHint: Used when an app is available from several sources. You can always change it on the app page.
settings.mockNotice: Demo mode – operations are only simulated.
settings.desktopNotice: Every package manager runs for real – installs are genuine. Developer package managers (npm, pip, Cargo…) are used in Developer mode.
settings.closeToTrayHint: Closing the window hides Unibox in the notification area next to the clock and running installs finish. Quit it from the icon's menu.
settings.closeBackgroundProcesses: Close an app running in the background without asking
settings.closeBackgroundProcessesHint: Before an install, update or uninstall, Unibox ends the app's processes that have no window (such as a tray icon or a process stuck in memory). An app with an open window gets a one-click offer to close it.
settings.advancedUninstall: Advanced uninstall with a leftover scan (registry and files)
settings.advancedUninstallHint: After an uninstall, it searches Program Files, ProgramData, Start menu and desktop shortcuts and the Windows registry (HKCU and HKLM\Software) besides AppData, and offers to delete the leftovers. Files go to the Recycle Bin; registry keys are backed up before they're deleted.
settings.autoCleanup: Remove leftover files and registry entries automatically, without a confirmation window
settings.autoCleanupHint: Leftovers are deleted right after the uninstall and you only get a short notification. Items in Program Files or HKLM need administrator rights – Windows asks once.
settings.newsCurrentHint: The window with new features shown after an update – in case you closed it by accident.
settings.trackInstallsHint: Before and after an install, Unibox compares folders (Program Files, ProgramData, AppData, Start menu, desktop) and the registry. Whatever the installer created is saved with the app and offered for removal after an uninstall – even without advanced uninstall. Installs take a few seconds longer. You can monitor a single app without this setting too: right-click → Install with monitoring.
settings.tracesHint: After an uninstall, the recorded items are offered for removal. Forgetting a record deletes nothing.
settings.managerPlanned: Desktop support is on the way
settings.devModeOnly: Developer package managers are used only in Developer mode – their packages then show up in search and among installed apps.
settings.managerPlannedError: Support for {{name}} in the desktop app is not ready yet.
settings.autostartHint: After you sign in, Unibox starts hidden in the notification area next to the clock and reports available updates.
settings.exportUniboxHint: All managed apps ({{count}}) with their settings – ignored and automatic updates and install options. JSON to import into Unibox, HTML as a readable page (which can be imported too).
settings.exportWingetHint: A JSON file for the winget import command ({{count}} apps from WinGet and the Microsoft Store).
settings.importAppsHint: A profile (.json, .html), a bundle (.ubundle) or a WinGet export – Unibox shows a summary and installs the missing apps in one click. Installed apps are skipped.

autoUpdates.autoCheckHint: In the background while Unibox runs (even hidden in the tray). The tray icon is blue during the check.
autoUpdates.autoInstallHint: Found updates are queued silently. Ignored, postponed and skipped updates are left out.
autoUpdates.selectedHint: You can also add them on an installed app's page (Update automatically).
autoUpdates.skipOnBatteryHint: Laptop unplugged – the install waits for the charger.
autoUpdates.skipOnSaver: Don't install while battery saver is on
autoUpdates.skipOnSaverHint: When battery saver is on in Windows (even when plugged in).
autoUpdates.skipOnMetered: Don't install on a metered connection
autoUpdates.skipOnMeteredHint: Mobile data, a hotspot or a connection set as metered in Windows. Unibox reports postponed updates and tries to install them again in 15 minutes.
autoUpdates.missed: If the scheduled time is missed
autoUpdates.missedHint: Unibox wasn't running at the time or the PC was asleep.
autoUpdates.minAgeHint: A new version is offered only after the set number of days since its release – time for bugs in fresh versions to get fixed. The release date comes from the Unibox catalog; for versions the catalog doesn't know, from when Unibox first saw them.
autoUpdates.warnHostChange: Warn when the installer host changes (WinGet)
autoUpdates.warnHostChangeHint: When the new version's installer is downloaded from a different host than the installed version's, the update is marked orange and isn't installed automatically. A different host may mean a hijacked package.
autoUpdates.stuckHint: Some packages are still offered after a successful update (the installer doesn't change the version in the registry). After the set number of attempts, such an update is no longer offered.
autoUpdates.preselectHint: Opening Updates checks them all – update them with one click in the bar at the bottom.
autoUpdates.optionsNote: An app's saved install options (as administrator, arguments, folder…) apply to its updates too – set them in Install options.
autoUpdates.trayNote: A failed automatic update switches the tray icon to the red state and is written to the notification history (bell).

security.warning: The following settings may pose a security risk, so they are disabled by default. Enable them IF AND ONLY IF you fully understand what they do and what consequences and dangers they may have.
security.elevationTitle: Change how operations request administrator rights
security.elevateAlways: Ask for administrator rights for every operation
security.elevateAlwaysHint: Every install, update and uninstall via WinGet and Chocolatey runs with administrator rights (UAC prompt). Scoop always runs without them.
security.elevateOnce: Ask for administrator rights only once
security.elevateOnceHint: After the first UAC confirmation, the elevated Unibox helper keeps running until the app exits and further operations are elevated without asking. It only accepts installs by id from official sources – anything else still needs UAC.
security.elevationProhibited: Prohibit any elevation via Unibox Elevator or Gsudo
security.elevationProhibitedHint: This option will cause problems. Any operation that can't elevate itself will fail.
security.broker: Delegate package operations to the Devolutions Agent broker
security.brokerHint: In companies with privilege management (Devolutions PEDM) the agent would run operations instead of Unibox. Unibox doesn't support delegation yet – so the switch is off; the check below shows the agent's state.
security.brokerWeb: Available only in the desktop app.
security.brokerDirect: operations run directly in Unibox (no broker)
security.allowCustomArgsHint: Install options will accept custom installer arguments. Without this the backend ignores them (arguments from Unibox options – PATH, no restart – keep working).
security.allowPrePost: Allow running custom pre-install and post-install commands
security.allowPrePostHint: Install options will accept commands (cmd) that run before and after the install – with your rights.
security.allowPaths: Allow changing package manager executable paths
security.allowPathsHint: Unibox uses the given winget.exe, choco.exe or scoop.ps1 instead of the one found in the system.
security.importCustomArgs: Allow importing custom command-line arguments when importing packages from a bundle
security.importCustomArgsHint: Otherwise custom arguments from the bundle file (.ubundle) are dropped.
security.importPrePost: Allow importing custom pre-install and post-install commands when importing packages from a bundle
security.importPrePostHint: Otherwise commands from the bundle file are dropped – a bundle from someone else can't run anything.

managerSetup.text: To install from {{name}}, the package manager itself needs to be installed first. Unibox does it with one click and then continues.
managerSetup.how: The official install script is used.
managerSetup.how_chocolatey: Uses the official script from chocolatey.org (community.chocolatey.org/install.ps1) – needs administrator rights (UAC prompt).
managerSetup.how_scoop: Uses the official installer from get.scoop.sh – for the current user, without administrator rights.
managerSetup.how_npm: Installs Node.js LTS, which includes npm, via WinGet.
managerSetup.how_pip: Installs Python 3.13, which includes pip, via WinGet.
managerSetup.how_cargo: Installs Rustup with Cargo via WinGet. Building most packages also needs Visual Studio Build Tools (C++).
managerSetup.how_vcpkg: vcpkg can’t be installed automatically: clone github.com/microsoft/vcpkg, run bootstrap-vcpkg.bat and set the VCPKG_ROOT variable.
managerSetup.installing: Installing {{name}}… this can take a minute.

appInUse.title: {{name}} is running
appInUse.text: The operation couldn't finish because {{name}} is running and the installer can't overwrite it.
appInUse.closeAndRetry: Close the app and try again
appInUse.notFound: The app's running processes weren't found – close it manually (including its tray icon) and try again.
appInUse.stubborn: The app didn't close (maybe it's waiting to save work). Save your work and close it, or force close it – unsaved changes will be lost.
appInUse.hint: The app is closed politely first – if it has unsaved data, it will ask to save.
appInUse.beforeText: {{kind}} would fail while {{name}} is running – the installer can't overwrite its files. Close it first; save any unsaved work.
